maya: Heads up — seeing a cluster-wide blip: several GPU nodes in us-west-2 flipped NotReady due to kubelet NetworkUnavailable and a few GPU pods got evicted. Autoscaler also scaled down a couple of jobs. Anyone else seeing this?

sanjay: Which nodes specifically? Any recent infra work (kernel, NIC firmware, CNI changes) in the us-west rollout?

maya: gpu-g1-21, gpu-g1-22, gpu-g1-34. We rolled a staged kernel update to ~20% of fleet this morning (5.19.11 -> 5.19.12). No CNI deploys.

eli: can you paste the kubelet/journal snippets and a `kubectl describe node` for one affected node?

maya: pasted below (condensed):

```
$ kubectl describe node gpu-g1-21
Name: gpu-g1-21
Conditions:
  Type    Status  LastHeartbeatTime            LastTransitionTime           Reason                  Message
  Ready   False   2024-12-11T10:26:29Z         2024-12-11T10:26:28Z        KubeletNotReady         kubelet is not ready: NetworkUnavailable
Non-terminated Pods:  38
Allocated resources: (gpu pods evicted)

$ journalctl -u kubelet -n 80 --no-pager
Dec 11 10:26:25 gpu-g1-21 kubelet[1472]: network health check failed: probe to 10.96.0.1:443 timed out
Dec 11 10:26:28 gpu-g1-21 kubelet[1472]: setting Node condition NetworkUnavailable
Dec 11 10:26:31 gpu-g1-21 kubelet[1472]: eviction manager: pod eviction threshold met, evicting pods
```

maya: ran some NIC checks on host:

```
# ip link show enp176s0f0
3: enp176s0f0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether 52:54:00:aa:bb:cc brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
# ip -s link show enp176s0f0
RX: bytes  packets  errors  dropped  overrun  mcast
    128345678  912345   0       211     0        0
TX: bytes  packets  errors  dropped  carrier collsns
    118345678  901234   0       0       0       0
# ethtool -S enp176s0f0 | head
rx_errs: 0
rx_no_buffer: 0
rx_missed: 213
```

eli: `rx_missed` is notable. Which CNI? calico-bpf? We saw MTU/jumbo issues before where fragmentation or offload toggles break probe traffic.

maya: yes, calico-bpf. Other non-upgraded nodes in same AZ are fine.

kube-probe-bot: alert: node gpu-g1-21 NetworkUnavailable -> NotReady (2024-12-11T10:26:28Z)

sanjay: any kernel/driver messages in dmesg? check `dmesg | grep -i offload` and `ethtool -k`. Also verify GSO/GRO/LRO state. These RDMA-capable NICs are sensitive to offload flags.

maya: ethtool output (affected vs healthy):

```
# ethtool -k enp176s0f0
segmentation-offload: on
generic-segmentation-offload: on
large-receive-offload: off    <-- affected node
# on healthy node
large-receive-offload: on
```

eli: bingo. LRO being off while other offloads vary can produce many small packets and driver-level missed RXs, causing intermittent probe timeouts. Kernel update likely toggled default offload behavior for this driver/hardware combo.

sanjay: that fits with the staged kernel rollout. Short-term mitigation options: mark nodes unschedulable, force kernel rollback on affected hosts, or toggle offload flags back on if supported.

maya: tried `ethtool -K enp176s0f0 gro on lro on` — kernel refuses LRO: "Operation not supported". Rebooted back to previous kernel (5.19.11) on gpu-g1-21 and LRO/GRO returned, kubelet probe succeeded, Node back to Ready and evicted pods rescheduled.

oncall-bot: incident-note: rolled back kernel on gpu-g1-21/22/34 -> 5.19.11; restarted calico daemonset; 3 evicted GPU pods rescheduled. No further evictions in 30m. P0 mitigated.

eli: long term: pin kernel for RDMA/NIC GPU pools until upstream vendor/kernel fix, file bug with NIC vendor and kernel team. Add a preflight check in the kernel rollout playbook to compare `ethtool -k` across a small canary set and alert on offload mismatches. Also consider suppressing autoscaler pod eviction thrash for brief NetworkUnavailable flaps during staged infra changes.

maya: created INFRA-1372 (kernel-regression, mtu-jumbo, calico-bpf) with logs, dmesg snippets, and rollback notes. Also added a runbook step: after kernel upgrade, verify GSO/GRO/LRO and compare to baseline before marking nodes healthy. Added an alert to detect ethtool offload mismatches across GPU node pool.

sanjay: thanks for quick triage. Summary for records: root cause = kernel/driver change that disabled LRO on RDMA-capable NICs; symptom = increased RX misses and east-west probe timeouts -> kubelet set NetworkUnavailable -> eviction manager removed pods. Mitigation = rollback kernel on affected nodes, restart networking components, update runbook and alerts. :white_check_mark:

maya: closing the loop — rolling rollback completed for staged hosts, infra ticket INFRA-1372 opened, monitoring added. :thumbsup:
